title: Bridge evals telemetry to Console alerts with config-change correlation and suppression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Evals discovered quality regressions are currently surfaced as raw signal events in the Evals service. Console receives these as undifferentiated alerts which cause noisy Slack/PagerDuty channels, duplicated tickets, and little context tying regressions to recent config or model changes.

Goal: Build a telemetry bridge that correlates eval regression signals with recent config/model change metadata, routes alerts into Console with richer context, and applies adaptive suppression/deduplication to reduce operational noise while preserving SLA-critical notices.

Proposed approach:
1) In Evals service, emit enriched regression events that include a change-fingerprint (hash of model_version + rollout_id + deployment_config) and a compact causal window (last 48h of related change events).
2) Console ingestion pipeline consumes these events, stores them in the eval-events index, and runs a lightweight correlation step to attach the most-likely change candidates.
3) Alerting logic: if multiple regressions map to the same change-fingerprint within a 2h sliding window, group into a single Console thread and send a single Slack block + 1 PagerDuty incident.
4) Suppression policy: soft-suppress follow-ups for 6h for grouped alerts unless severity escalates or customers report incidents.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We must avoid blocking the evals ingestion path; correlation should be eventually consistent and idempotent.
- Deduplication heuristics must favor recall over precision initially to avoid missing distinct regressions. We will tune thresholds after initial rollout.
- Adding change-fingerprint requires coordination with PM and model rollout services to commit to a canonical metadata schema.

Stakeholders: PM (Jade Moreno), Product (Sanjay Rao), Console eng (Marcus Liu), Evals eng (Tomoko Sato), DevEx (Nina Gomez), SRE (Oliver Brown).
acceptance_criteria: Console receives enriched eval regression events including change-fingerprint and causal window metadata.
Regression alerts with the same change-fingerprint within the correlation window are grouped into a single Console thread.
Grouped alerts post one consolidated Slack message and create at most one PagerDuty incident per group unless severity escalates.
A telemetry dashboard shows pre/post correlation alert volume and reduction percentage (target >= 40% noise reduction in first 30 days).
Documentation updated: Console runbook includes dedupe logic, suppression policy, and tuning knobs.
Automated QA: integration test that simulates multiple eval regressions tied to a single config change and verifies consolidation behavior.
technical_notes: change-fingerprint = sha1(model_version + '|' + rollout_id + '|' + minimal_config_json). We will canonicalize config ordering and drop non-deterministic fields.
Correlation service implemented as idempotent consumer that writes a grouping key to eval-events index and emits a grouped-alert event if key is new.
Use existing Console rate-limiter + dedupe index (console-alerts-v2) to avoid re-implementing TTLs; add new field 'grouping_key'.
Suppression policy initially configured: window=6h, sliding-group=2h, escalation threshold=2x baseline severity. Tunable via Console feature flag.
Performance: correlation step must not add >50ms median latency to Console ingestion pipeline; fallback to queue if overloaded.
Data retention: keep grouped mapping for 30 days to support retrospective evaluation and rollback tracing.

risk: False positives in grouping could hide distinct regressions if rollout metadata is incomplete. Operational risk if suppression policy hides critical incidents. Mitigations: conservative default grouping, visible suppression metadata in Slack thread, manual override to reopen suppressed flows.
